extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom leaders, media-industry observers, and informed readers interested in journalism ethics and AI in news
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and evaluative criteria for producing or assessing AI-assisted local news sites and experiments, with emphasis on attribution, editorial oversight, accuracy, and legal/commercial transparency. Focused on how AI tools are used in newsroom workflows and public-facing content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to original journalists and outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories and photographs must credit the original reporters and outlets when drawing from or republishing their work; Poynter found more than 70 stories that included reporting, writing and photography from local journalists without attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give credit where credit is due; do not republish or closely rework another outlet's reporting without explicit attribution or permission. The article quotes local journalists saying it would be 'nice for any outlet … to give credit where credit is due.' Examples of failures include removing references to the original outlet and presenting paraphrased material as original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use only appropriate source material (public civic info vs other news reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated stories were supposed to be based on publicly available civic information (press releases, meeting videos), but many were generated from other news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit AI inputs to genuinely public civic documents and primary-source materials when the intent is to summarize public information. Avoid using other outlets' reporting as the primary source for generated articles unless properly attributed and permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear disclosure of AI use and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the Nota News pages disclosed how they used AI; the sites noted they were 'Powered by Nota News and Springwire.ai' but did not explain usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-facing projects should clearly disclose when AI generated or assisted content, and how AI was used (e.g., drafting from transcripts, summarizing press releases). 'Powered by' labels alone are insufficient—explain scope, limitations, and whether human oversight occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal, written editorial guidelines and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Nota News lacked clear editorial guidelines and formal oversight; contractors said 'They don’t have anything on paper. They don’t have rules. They don’t have manuals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain written editorial policies, documented workflows, and clear sign-offs. Ensure editors or senior leadership review AI-generated pieces before publication and that standards are communicated to contractors and staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment vs public product boundary (do not expose experiments as live news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Company leaders called the sites 'live experiments' and 'digital brochures' not meant for the public, but Nota issued a press release and promoted the initiative publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conducting experiments, keep them private or clearly label them as non-public test environments; do not publish experimental outputs in ways that could be indexed, promoted, or treated as independent news sources without appropriate safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image rights and photo attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter identified more than 30 images on Nota News copied from other sites without proper rights or attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat photos as clearly copyright-protected—obtain licenses or permissions and credit sources. Do not republish images from other outlets without explicit rights; copying photos is more straightforwardly actionable under copyright law than some text uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and timeliness verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Nota News republished a story reporting that a bill had just passed when it had passed two years earlier—showing failures in checking timeliness and factual accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify dates, current status of legislation/events, and timeliness before publishing. AI summaries should be cross-checked against primary-source timelines and contemporary coverage to avoid presenting outdated information as new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper handling of quotations and attribution of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where quotes were paraphrased or summarized but still presented in quotation marks, and where references to original outlets were removed or misrepresented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use direct quotation marks for verbatim quotes; when paraphrasing, do not present paraphrase as a quote. Preserve and clearly attribute the source of quotes and unique reporting obtained by other journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid introducing AI-generated errors or hallucinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nota News added errors likely generated by AI (e.g., shortening Georgia O’Keeffe to 'Ga. O’Keeffe', spelling 'K-9' as 'K-nine').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute human fact-checking to catch hallucinations, formatting errors, and odd paraphrases introduced by models. Do not publish generated text without review for factual and stylistic correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about training data and customer-data use
rubrics_metrics.description: Company statements about training Polaris on 'rights-cleared data' and customer data raised questions; Brandau said Nota does not train models on customer data by default but some clients granted permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose what data was used to train models (high-level) and whether client or third-party content was included. Clarify default policies and obtain informed consent when customer data will be used to train models that could reproduce their content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not repurpose client content without explicit permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Some clients' content appeared on Nota News (e.g., outlets listed as customers whose reporting was reused), raising questions about internal safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat client content with contractual and ethical protections; never reuse or republish client-produced journalism in product demos, experiments, or training data without explicit permission or clear contractual allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution when summarizing or using press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter found Nota News took content from press releases without attribution and then sometimes added AI-generated errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When summarizing press releases or public documents, attribute the source and verify factual statements rather than relying on a generator to paraphrase without context. Make clear when content is derived from a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable production quotas that do not sacrifice quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial staff were given very high quotas (10–15 stories per day per editor) and pressure to emphasize quantity over quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set realistic output expectations that allow time for sourcing, verification, attribution, and editorial review. Quotas should not incentivize cutting corners or using other outlets' reporting as shortcut sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of local expertise and community context
rubrics_metrics.description: Local journalists argued AI misses community perspective and backstory; coverage produced cheaply risks losing context that experienced local reporters provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure local knowledge and context are incorporated—either via local hires/editors or rigorous research—rather than relying solely on AI summaries that cannot replicate lived community understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent monetization and reader-facing fundraising
rubrics_metrics.description: One Nota News site included a donations page saying 'Every contribution strengthens local journalism' though Brandau said Nota did not receive money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about monetization—if asking for donations, clearly state who receives funds and how they will be used. Avoid implying support for community journalism if the entity is an experimental or commercial product that does not deliver journalistic services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear role definitions and training for contractors and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors reported low pay ($30/hour), lack of guidance, and confusion over whether their work was 'journalistic' or experimental product work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define roles, responsibilities, and expectations in contracts; provide training on editorial standards, attribution, copyright, and acceptable AI practices; ensure fair pay and clarity about publication and bylines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance with copyright and intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright law protects original works whether seen by zero or millions; copying text and especially photos can violate copyright regardless of audience size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess reproductions for fair use and obtain licenses when required. Treat copying of articles and images as potential copyright infringement; legal counsel and rights clearance processes should be part of workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior leadership accountability and pre-publication guardrails
rubrics_metrics.description: Company leaders acknowledged failures and said they would implement stricter guardrails and more oversight from senior leadership after the issue surfaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish senior-level review, incident response plans, and pre-publication checks for novel uses of AI; leadership should own and enforce editorial standards and remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest bylines and role transparency (do not misattribute authorship)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generated articles appeared under the bylines of staff who later said they did not view the work as traditional journalism; one story used 'NewsDesk' as byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attribute AI-generated or heavily AI-assisted content to a reporter who did not perform the core reporting and verification. Make bylines and author roles transparent (e.g., 'Generated by [tool], edited by [person]') and avoid implying original reporting when content is aggregated or synthesized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate translation processes for bilingual content
rubrics_metrics.description: Spanish versions were created with Google Translate rather than professional translation and publishing processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional translators or rigorous human review when publishing in other languages. Automatic translation without review can introduce errors and cultural/contextual inaccuracies; do not rely on raw machine translation for publication.
